 Judgment

The present appeal is filed by the appellants/claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 06.05.2015 in MVC.No.2640/2012 passed by VIII Addl. Small Causes Judge and MACT (SCCH-5),
Bengaluru, questioning the attribution of 30% of contributory negligence on the part of the deceased and also for seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.text:
VIII Addl. Small Causes Judge and MACT (SCCH-5),
Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts of the case are that, on 04.03.2012 when the deceased-Manjunatha was moving from Beechaganahalli village on his TVS Max No.KA-40-R-2797 another vehicle bearing No.KA-01-MD-6330 driven in a rash and negligent manner had struck the two wheeler from rear side, resulting in death of the deceased- Manjunatha.

3. Heard the arguments from both sides and perused the records.
4.

Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants submitted that the finding of the Tribunal is that the deceased has also attributed 30% of contributory negligence because of the fact that the deceased has not worn headgear, hence, contributory negligence cannot be sustained, since that finding is only speculative in nature.
Therefore, submitted that the rash and negligent aspect is to be ascertained as to who was driving the vehicle rashly and negligently.
Therefore, submitted that the said finding is not correct.
Further submitted that the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lesser side.
Therefore, prays for enhancement of compensation.

Learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company placed reliance on the judgment of this Court in the case of The Oriental Insurance Co., Ltd., Vs. Sri Naresh Babu N., and Others1.
8.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co., Ltd., Vs. Sri Naresh Babu N., and Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: By placing reliance on the above said judgments, learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company argued that this Court on the reason that the deceased had not worn helmet and also the deceased was not holding driving licence to drive the vehicle, therefore, MFA.No.7074/2016 DD.06.12.2017 attributing entire negligence on the part of the deceased, thus allowed the appeal filed by the Insurance Company.
Therefore, submitted that, the present case also, it is squarely covered by the above stated judgments.
Therefore, prays to dismiss the appeal.
9. The factum of accident and death of the deceased is not disputed.
The Tribunal had observed that the deceased had not worn helmet and if the deceased had worn helmet, then the deceased might not have died.

Therefore, opined that non-wearing of helmet is also contributory factor, hence,
fastened 30% of contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
Further opined that the deceased was not possessing driving licence.
Therefore, this is also one of the contributory factor.
Thus, it is held that the deceased also contributed his negligence towards the accident.
But upon considering the accident occurred, the accident is between car and motorcycle.

The deceased was driving the motor cycle bearing No.KA-40-R- 2797 and at that time, the car bearing No.KA-01-MD-6330 dashed the motor cycle and caused the accident inviting into death of the deceased.
Therefore, in this regard, the driver who was driving the vehicle rashly and negligently is to be considered.
Non-wearing of helmet is the secondary factor to be considered.
But who has driven the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and caused the accident is to be considered as a primary aspect.
Whether the deceased worn helmet or not and because of non-wearing of helmet only, the death was caused is to be considered as secondary aspect.
In the complaint, it is alleged against the driver of the car who drove the car in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased and the deceased died.
10. As per the record issued by the NIMHANS Hospital, it is shown that the deceased had not worn helmet at the time of the accident.
But as discussed above, who was driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner is to be ascertained.
The entire allegation in the complaint is against the driver of the car.
The result of investigation culminated into filing of charge sheet against the driver of the car.
Just because, the deceased had not worn helmet and if he had worn helmet, then death could have been avoided is a speculative in nature.
Therefore, in this regard, attributing contributory negligence on the part of the deceased cannot be sustained.

The Division Bench of this Court in a similar set of facts and circumstances in the case of Mallavva Laxman Terani and others Vs.
North-West Karnataka State Transport Corporation, Belagavi2 (hereinafter referred to as Mallavva Laxman Terani's case), had observed that whether the rider of the bike would have survived, if he had worn headgear is a speculative question, which this Court cannot answer with the precision.

sentences.text: Therefore, upon considering the evidence on record, it is proved that due to rash and negligent driving of the car, the accident was caused and the deceased died.
May be non-wearing of helmet is the violation of provision also, but it is the safeguard to the head of the driver of the motor cycle.

Just because, the deceased was injured,
non- wearing of helmet cannot be made as contributory negligence as stated above and also as held by the Division Bench of this Court in Mallavva Laxman Terani's case, the said question is a speculative question.

11. It must be proved by the Insurance Company that because of non-wearing of helmet only the deceased died and also ought to have been proved that the deceased was rash and negligent in driving the vehicle and the said rash and negligent cannot be attributed for not wearing helmet.
Therefore, the Tribunal has committed error in attributing 30% of contributory negligence on the - 11 - part of the deceased.
It is also for the reason that non-holding of driving licence by the deceased has not been proved, hence, attributing contributory negligence is not proper and correct.

The aspects of wearing helmet or non-wearing of helmet or possessing driving licence or not is to be ascertained after proving that the driver of the offending vehicle was rash and negligent, where it is proved that the driver of the offending vehicle, which in the present case, driver of the car bearing No.KA-01-MD- 6330 is found to be rash and negligent, then attributing contributory negligence on the part of the deceased for non-wearing helmet and not holding driving licence cannot be sustained.

Therefore, the rash and negligent aspect is to be considered on the actions of drivers, but not in passive way by not wearing helmet and not in possession of driving licence, so what would be the direct action means who was driving the vehicle and whether he was rash and negligent that can be considered, but not in a passive way as above stated.
Therefore, the Tribunal is - 12 - not correct in holding that the deceased also contributed 30% of negligence.
The said finding is to be set aside.
Accordingly, it is set aside.
Regarding quantum of compensation:

12. The Tribunal has awarded the compensation under various heads as follows:
1 Loss of dependency Rs. 10,08,000/- 2 Loss of consortium Rs. 20,000/- 3 Loss of love and affection Rs. 40,000/- 4 Loss of estate Rs. 50,000/- 5

Funeral expenses Rs.
15,000/-
 TOTAL Rs. 11,33,000/-
 Deducted 30% towards Rs. 8,70,600/-

notional income at Rs.7,000/- pm., is to be taken into consideration as per - 13 - the Notional Income Chart recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
The Tribunal has committed error in considering the income at Rs.6,000/- pm.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi3 and also decision of this Court in the case of New India Assurance Company Vs. Abdul S/o Mehaboob Tahasildar4 as the deceased was aged 26 years, 40% of income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life.

sentences.text: As the deceased was aged 26 years as on the date of the accident, the appropriate multiplier applicable is 17.

Hence, the compensation under the head loss of dependency is re-assessed and quantified as follows:
Rs.7,000/- + Rs.2,800/- (40% of Rs.7,000/-)=Rs.9,800/- Rs.9,800/- x  x 17 x12=Rs.14,99,400/- (2017) 16 SCC 680 MFA.NO.103807/2016 C/W MFA.NOS.103835/2016 & 103807/2018 DD.27.05.2022 - 14 -
Accordingly, compensation of Rs.14,99,400/- is awarded under the head loss of dependency.
14. The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head loss of consortium and Rs.40,000/- under the head loss of love and affection.
The loss of love and affection and loss of consortium are having the same connotation.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Limited v. Nanu Ram & Others5, each claimants are entitled for Rs.40,000/- with 10% escalation under the head loss of consortium.

compensation of Rs.1,76,000/- (Rs.40,000/- x 4 + 10% escalation) is awarded under the head loss of consortium including loss of love and affection.
The compensation of Rs.15,000/- is awarded under the head loss of estate as against Rs.50,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
16. The compensation of Rs.15,000/- awarded under the head funeral expenses is found to be correct.
Hence, it is kept in tact.
